title: Land Transport and Related Matters Bill
what_it_is: Land Transport and Related Matters Bill

sections.label: Joint MOT MHA Bill
sections.summary: A joint Bill by MOT and MHA covers several key areas, including ERP 2.0 and penalties for serious vehicular offences.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: It is also a joint Bill by the Ministry of Transport (MOT) and the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) covering several key areas.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: I will speak on amendments pertaining to the Electronic Road Pricing (ERP) 2.0 system and increasing penalties for serious vehicular offences.

sections.label: OBU toll and parking payments
sections.summary: Clauses 59 to 64 simplify settlement processes and decriminalise missed ERP charges, currently an offence under the Road Traffic Act.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Soon, motorists will be able to use the OBU for contactless toll payments at land checkpoints as well as for roadside electronic parking.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: This is why we are introducing clauses 59 to 64 in this Bill to simplify settlement processes and to decriminalise missed ERP charges, which are currently an offence under the Road Traffic Act.

sections.label: OBU mandatory for vehicles
sections.summary: On 1 January 2027, when ERP 2.0 is fully rolled out and ERP 1.0 decommissioned, the OBU will be mandatory for all Singapore-registered vehicles.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: On 1 January 2027, when the ERP 2.0 is completely rolled out and ERP 1.0 is decommissioned, the OBU will be mandatory for all Singapore-registered vehicles.

sections.label: OBU tampering and modification penalties
sections.summary: The Bill makes unauthorised OBU tampering, modification, services and advertising offences, with penalties up to $20,000 and/or two years' imprisonment, doubled for repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: To safeguard the integrity of the ERP 2.0 system, it will be an offence to tamper with or modify OBUs without authorisation, and provide or advertise services on the OBU similarly without authorisation.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: For serious cases of deliberate non-compliance or misuse, the legislation provides for penalties of up to $20,000 and/or imprisonment of up to two years.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Today, there are over 1,000 cases of illegal vehicle modifications detected annually.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: And to deter workshops from doing illegal modification on a large scale, clause 52 of the Bill raises the maximum penalties for such illegal alterations.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Under the Bill, individuals can face fines up to $20,000 and/or imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years, with penalties doubled for repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: For non-individuals, first time offenders can be fined up to $40,000, and up to $80,000 for repeat offenders.

sections.label: Mobility vehicle and scooter rules
sections.summary: The speed limit for mobility vehicles on public paths will be lowered to six kilometres an hour, and mobility scooter users must be certified to have a medical need.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: First, we will lower the speed limit for mobility vehicles on public paths to six kilometres an hour.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Third, we will require that users of mobility scooters be certified to have a medical need for the device, in order to ride a mobility scooter on public paths.

sections.label: Rules effective June 2026
sections.summary: After this Bill, the rules are intended to take effect from 1 June 2026 to give stakeholders transition time.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: To give stakeholders sufficient transition time after this Bill, we intend for the rules to take effect from 1 June 2026.

sections.label: Mobility vehicle speed penalties
sections.summary: From 1 June 2026, selling or riding mobility vehicles above six kilometres per hour carries fines or imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: At six kilometres per hour, mobility vehicles match the pace of a brisk walker, which meet the needs of genuine users who have difficulty walking.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: This means that from 1 June 2026, selling mobility vehicles with a device speed limit above six kilometres per hour will carry penalties of up to $20,000 or imprisonment up to 24 months, or both, with higher penalties for non-individuals and repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: An individual who rides or drives a mobility vehicle at a speed exceeding six kilometres per hour on a public path will face fines of up to $2,000 or up to six months' imprisonment, or both, with higher penalties for repeat violations.

sections.label: PMA size and weight limits
sections.summary: From 1 June 2026, PMAs must not exceed set width, length, height and laden weight limits.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: From 1 June 2026, PMAs must not exceed a width of 70 centimetres, a length of 120 centimetres, a height of 150 centimetres and a laden weight of 300 kilogrammes.

sections.label: Mobility scooter medical need rule
sections.summary: From 1 June 2026, only those with genuine medical need may ride mobility scooters on public paths.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Third, to curb misuse, only those with genuine medical need will be allowed to ride a mobility scooter on public paths from 1 June 2026.

sections.label: Clinic certification fees
sections.summary: LTA's survey of clinics found fees expected to range from $20 to $150, with a median of $50.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Based on LTA's survey of clinics, fees are expected to range from $20 to $150, with a median fee of $50.

sections.label: Certificate of Medical Need requirement
sections.summary: From 1 June 2026, mobility scooter users on public paths must have a Certificate of Medical Need, with penalties for non-compliance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: From 1 June 2026, mobility scooter users on public paths must have this Certificate of Medical Need.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Users will have the next three months to obtain the certification, and enforcement officers will engage and educate users on these new rules during this transition period.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Those caught riding a mobility scooter on public paths without the Certificate of Medical Need will face penalties of up to $2,000 in fines or imprisonment of up to six months, or both.

sections.label: Mobility scooter registration phases
sections.summary: Registration starts for mobility scooters sold from 1 June 2026, and all mobility scooters from 1 January 2029.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: To give users time to adjust to the rule, we will implement the registration regime in phases and keep the process user-friendly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We will start by requiring registration for mobility scooters sold from 1 June 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Thereafter, from 1 January 2029, all mobility scooters will need to be registered before they can be used on a public path.

sections.label: PMA user exemptions
sections.summary: Exemptions from the Certificate of Medical Need requirement will apply to seniors and existing Government scheme beneficiaries, recognising PMA users' mobility challenges.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: In designing our regulations, we also recognise the unique needs of PMA users, who have mobility challenges.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: This is why we will implement exemptions from the Certificate of Medical Need requirement for seniors and existing Government scheme beneficiaries.

sections.label: AMD-related fires in 2025
sections.summary: In 2025, 49 AMD-related fires were recorded.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: In 2025 alone, we recorded 49 AMD-related fires.

sections.label: Amendments on unsafe devices
sections.summary: Clauses 84 to 91 will amend the Small Motorised Vehicles (Safety) Act 2020 to prohibit keeping unsafe devices.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Clauses 84 to 91 will amend the Small Motorised Vehicles (Safety) Act 2020 to prohibit the keeping of unsafe devices.

sections.label: Penalties for offences
sections.summary: Penalties include fines up to $2,000 or imprisonment up to three months, or both, with higher penalties for non-individuals and repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Penalties include fines up to $2,000 or imprisonment up to three months, or both, with higher penalties for non-individuals and repeat offenders.

sections.label: Lorry speed limiter installation
sections.summary: As of 5 January 2026, around 72% of lorries required to have speed limiters installed by the various deadlines had done so.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: As of 5 January 2026, around 72% of lorries required to have speed limiters installed by the various deadlines have done so.

sections.label: Increased maximum fines
sections.summary: The Bill increases maximum fines to $10,000 for a first conviction and $20,000 for subsequent convictions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The Bill updates the penalty framework by increasing the maximum fines to $10,000 for a first conviction and $20,000 for subsequent convictions.

sections.label: Court disqualification period length
sections.summary: The Court may impose any disqualification period at or above the prescribed minimum, including lifetime disqualification.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The disqualification period that the Court may impose can be any period equal to or above the prescribed minimum disqualification period, including a lifetime disqualification period if it thinks fit.

sections.label: No special reasons needed
sections.summary: The amendments clarify that no special reasons are needed before a Court imposes a disqualification longer than the prescribed minimum.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The amendments make it clear that there is no need for special reasons before a Court may impose a disqualification period that is longer than the prescribed minimum period.

sections.label: SAF vehicle exemption and civilian processing
sections.summary: The amendment clarifies the exemption applies to SAF-owned or leased vehicles, and Clauses 74 and 79 let authorised civilians process such violations with safeguards.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The amendment makes it clear that the exemption applies to vehicles owned or leased by SAF.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Clauses 74 and 79 amend the Road Traffic Act to allow processing of such violations to be carried out by authorised civilians, including service providers, subject to appropriate safeguards.

sections.label: Discretionary forfeiture of road vehicles
sections.summary: Forfeiture becomes discretionary in all scenarios if it is proved the offender was not the owner and used the vehicle without consent.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The amendment will make the forfeiture of road vehicles discretionary in all scenarios if it is proved to the Court's satisfaction that the person who committed the scheduled offence involving the vehicle is not the vehicle owner and had used the vehicle without the consent of its owner.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: MHA remains concerned by the road safety situation and has plans to further tighten our laws and regulatory framework.

sections.label: PAP MPs speaking on regulations
sections.summary: A total of 18 PAP MPs will speak on new regulations on PMAs, ERP 2.0, vehicle safety and related issues.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: A total of 18 PAP Members of Parliament (MPs) will speak on the new regulations on PMAs, ERP 2.0, vehicle safety and other related issues.

sections.label: OBU installation completion timeline
sections.summary: Although most vehicles now have OBUs, full installation is only expected to complete by 2027, a gap of at least seven years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Although most vehicles now have OBUs, full installation is only expected to complete by 2027, at least seven-year gap from original approval to completion.

sections.label: PMA speed limits and medical certificate
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the Bill's measures to limit PMA speeds and require a Certificate of Medical Need, citing danger to frail and elderly pedestrians.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: But the point is that such irresponsible use is dangerous to other pedestrians, especially when we have many frail and elderly residents using that walkway.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Hence, I welcome the Bill’s measures to limit PMA speeds and to require a Certificate of Medical Need.

sections.label: Cameras improved pedestrian bridge compliance
sections.summary: After temporary cameras were installed in 2024 on the pedestrian bridge between Paya Lebar Way and Aljunied Crescent in MacPherson, compliance improved.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: For example, after temporary cameras were installed in 2024 on the pedestrian bridge between Paya Lebar Way and Aljunied Crescent in MacPherson, compliance improved.

sections.label: UL2272 and EN14194 fire safety standards
sections.summary: The speaker supports making possession of non-UL2272 e-scooters an offence, saying UL2272 and EN14194 standards reduced fire risks from charging.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: In addition, requiring PMDs and PABs to meet the UL2272 and EN14194 standards has been a prudent safety measure that reduced fire risks from charging.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: This is a positive outcome, but more can be done to keep fires down further.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Hence, I support making the possession of non-UL2272 e-scooters an offence.

sections.label: Bill balances mobility and risk
sections.summary: The speaker says the Bill strikes a sensible balance between enabling mobility and managing risks, while keeping spaces open and protecting the vulnerable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Co-existence is key to living in a diverse and highly built-up Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: We need to keep spaces open for all to live, work and play, but we must also intervene to support or protect the vulnerable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Overall, this Bill strikes a sensible balance between enabling mobility and managing the risks that come with new usage patterns and technologies.

sections.label: ERP 2.0 data as court evidence
sections.summary: Under clause 81, a document certified by the registrar containing transaction and location data from ERP 2.0 devices is admissible as evidence in court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Under clause 81, a document certified by the registrar containing transaction and location data from ERP 2.0 devices will be admissible as evidence in court.

sections.label: New PMA rules and limits
sections.summary: The Bill introduces a Certificate of Medical Need requirement, dimension limits and reduces the mobility scooter speed limit from 10 to six kilometres per hour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Yet, even as enforcement resources remain limited, this Bill introduces more changes, more rules and changes for PMAs: implementing the Certificate of Medical Need requirement, imposing dimension limits and reducing the speed limit for mobility scooters from 10 kilometres per hour to six kilometres per hour.

sections.label: HDB fires caused by AMDs
sections.summary: Minister Shanmugam said 187 HDB estate fires were caused by AMDs, 46% by PMDs, 42% by PABs and 12% by PMAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In a September 2025 Parliamentary Question reply, Minister Shanmugam said that 187 fires in Housing and Development Board (HDB) estates were caused by AMDs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Of these 46% by PMDs, 42% by PABs and 12% for PMAs.

sections.label: Mobility scooter speed limit concerns
sections.summary: Reducing the mobility scooter speed limit to six kilometres per hour raises concerns, which the speaker has previously addressed in this House.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The reduction of mobility scooter speed limit to six kilometres per hour raises some concerns, and I have spoken on this in this House previously.

sections.label: Seniors exempted from certification requirement
sections.summary: The Government decided to exempt seniors aged 70 and above from the certification requirement, which the speaker had urged reconsidering.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: At the 2024 Committee of Supply debate for MOT, I had urged the Government in the run-up to the introduction of the new PMD regime to reconsider permitting seniors aged at least 67 or 70 to be allowed to use mobility scooters, even in the absence of a formerly diagnosed musculoskeletal or medical condition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I am glad that the Government has decided to exempt seniors aged 70 and above from the certification requirement.

sections.label: Enforcement against PMA users
sections.summary: MHA said notices and fines up to $2,000 were issued with few prosecutions, and 10 PMA road users were caught in 2024 versus four in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: MHA revealed that while notices were issued and fines of up to $2,000 were imposed, the number of formal prosecutions was relatively low, often handled through compensation fines first.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In another reply to my Parliamentary Question in 2024, MHA also confirmed that enforcement against PMA users on roads had increased with 10 users caught between January and August 2024, compared to four in 2023.

sections.label: PMA riders' earnings and platform commitments
sections.summary: A rider expects earnings to fall 30% to 40% under the speed limit, and platform associations obtained commitments to review delivery targets and work arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Based on her experience, she expects her earnings to fall by 30% to 40% under the six kilometres per hour speed limit if incentives and work conditions are not adjusted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: As worker representatives, our platform work associations, including the NDCA, have raised these concerns directly with platform operators.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: We have since obtained commitments and in-principle agreements from platform partners through bilateral negotiations to review delivery targets and work arrangements for our full-time PMA riders, so that safety improvements do not come at the expense of livelihoods.

sections.label: NDCA subsidising medical certification costs
sections.summary: Medical certification costs $50 to $100, and the NDCA will provide financial assistance to subsidise and co-pay members' out-of-pocket compliance costs under this Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Medical certification can range from $50 to $100, which is significant for lower-income riders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: To support our members, the NDCA will provide financial assistance to help subsidise and co-pay out-of-pocket compliance costs arising from this Act.

sections.label: Platform workers transition support
sections.summary: NDCA works with platform operators through a tripartite framework to mitigate livelihood impact, and Grab gave in-principle assurances to adjust performance targets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: It reflects lived realities and this is why NDCA continues to work closely with platform operators through the tripartite framework to mitigate livelihood impact while complying to these new rules.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: We thank our platform operators partners, like Grab, who have given in-principle assurances to adjust performance targets, and NDCA will continue to support riders through the transition to defray costs, including medical certification and device modifications.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   By 2030, electric buses will make up half of our public bus fleet.

sections.label: Speed limits for vehicles
sections.summary: Passenger vehicles may travel up to 90 kilometres per hour and heavy vehicles are capped at 60 kilometres per hour.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Passenger vehicles may travel at up to 90 kilometres per hour, while heavy vehicles are capped at 60 kilometres per hour.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Local operators who comply with speed-limiter requirements may find themselves disadvantaged when foreign-registered heavy vehicles, which may not be subjected to the same standards, continue travelling at higher speeds.

sections.label: PMA speed limit reduction
sections.summary: The Bill proposes reducing the PMA speed limit from 10 kilometres per hour to six kilometres per hour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Bill proposes to reduce the speed limit for PMAs from 10 kilometres per hour to six kilometres per hour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In an article published by Mothership on 27 January, platform workers shared that this reduction in speed limit is likely to reduce the orders they can complete by 20% to 30%, or even up to 50%.

sections.label: Community bus shuttle seed funding
sections.summary: The Ministry is encouraged to offer seed funding to pilot community bus shuttles in towns including Kaki Bukit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Furthermore, Mr Speaker, I would encourage the Ministry to offer seed funding to pilot and test community bus shuttles in different towns, including Kaki Bukit, with the intention of providing coverage for those short but significant journeys around the neighbourhood that are currently underserved by our public transport operators.

sections.label: Public transport for ageing population
sections.summary: These improvements would make the public transport network more fit for purpose for the ageing population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This may reduce their reliance on mobility devices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These improvements would also make our public transport network more fit for purpose for our ageing population.

sections.label: Merdeka Pass for seniors
sections.summary: A Merdeka Pass is proposed for seniors to travel freely on public transport, similar to the Freedom Pass.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Over there, they call it the "Freedom Pass".

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I see no reason why we cannot or should not do the same for our seniors and give them a Merdeka Pass to travel freely on our public transport.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   We need to prioritise improvements to public transport links, including boosting capacity for last mile connectivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I also suggest that MOT establish seed funding to study and test "community bus" services in towns like Kaki Bukit.

sections.label: Segregating pedestrians from mobility devices
sections.summary: Pedestrian safety is best achieved by separating pedestrians from motor-powered mobility devices through dedicated cycling paths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Ultimately, if pedestrian safety is our concern, this is best achieved by segregating pedestrian traffic from motor-powered mobility devices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We can achieve this by moving more decisively towards a more coherent and integrated network of dedicated cycling paths that are clearly separated from pedestrian footpaths, wherever possible and then confining the use of mobility devices to these cycling paths.

sections.label: Reclaiming road space for cycling
sections.summary: The Government should reconsider reclaiming road space from cars and repurposing it for cycling and walking infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Since we expect private vehicle growth to be capped as car-lite policies take effect, the Government should seriously reconsider reclaiming road space currently dedicated to cars, including underutilised lanes and on-street parking – and repurposing them for cycling and walking infrastructure.

sections.label: Tightening PMA user rules
sections.summary: The Bill's amendments to tighten PMA users' eligibility, operating rules and specifications are overdue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: The Bill's amendments to tighten PMA users' eligibility, operating rules and specifications are overdue.

sections.label: Younger people unable to walk
sections.summary: Some younger people cannot walk far due to weight or conditions like gout but cannot obtain a doctor's certificate of eligibility.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: While 70 years old may be a reasonable eligible age for automatic eligibility, there are also many instances of younger people who are unable to walk far due to excessive weight or temporary conditions such as gout but are unable to obtain a doctor's certificate of eligibility.

sections.label: Extending conditional PMA eligibility
sections.summary: LTA should consider extending conditional PMA user eligibility to this group if they have no past speeding offences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: While this may be a small group, I hope that LTA will consider extending conditional PMA user eligibility to them if they have not chalked up speeding offences in the past.

sections.label: Workshop on responsible PMA use
sections.summary: LTA could consider a basic workshop or course on responsible use to reduce anti-social PMA users.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: In addition to eligibility criteria, can LTA consider a basic workshop or course on responsible use so as to reduce instances of anti-social PMA users?

sections.label: PMD and PMA rules
sections.summary: Rules start 1 June 2026; about 5,100 PMDs are registered and retailers report rising PMA sales.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: The rules will kick in from 1 June 2026.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: PMDs, however, do need to be registered and currently, there are about 5,100 of these.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: While we do not know how many PMAs there are, retailers have reported increasing sales of hundreds of PMAs each year.

sections.label: Neighbours and LTA confiscation powers
sections.summary: Neighbours can inform LTA of parked PMAs and e-scooters, and the passage asks if LTA can confiscate non-compliant items.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: The neighbours of these PMAs and e-scooters owners are a useful source of accurate information of where and when these PMAs and e-scooters are parked which would be valuable information source to LTA enforcement officers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Also, should the non-compliant PMAs or e-scooters owners refuse to remove them, are LTA enforcement officers vested with the powers to confiscate these items?

sections.label: Certificate of Medical Need exemptions
sections.summary: LTA's OneMotoring site listed exemptions from the Certificate of Medical Need, including users aged 70 and above.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Complicating this is that I understand that LTA's OneMotoring site listed several exemptions from the Certificate of Medical Need.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: These include users aged 70 and above, beneficiaries of the Assistive Technology Fund and Seniors Mobility Enabling Fund, and individuals assessed to require assistance with ADL under various assessments.

sections.label: Disabled People's Association implementation period
sections.summary: The Disabled People's Association said a one- to two-year implementation period would be more comparable to other laws.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Disabled People's Association highlighted this point in their comments on this Bill, stating that a one- to two-year implementation period would be more comparable to other laws, such as the Workplace Fairness Act.

sections.label: Data for six kilometre speed limit
sections.summary: The passage asks what data shows reducing the speed limit to six kilometres an hour reduces serious injury risk.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Can the Minister of State share what is the actual data used to determine how reducing the speed limit to six kilometres an hour is significantly more likely to reduce the risk of serious injury, affect reflex time and prevent more accidents to begin with?

sections.label: Graduated penalties for repeat offenders
sections.summary: The passage suggests a more graduated and targeted approach to penalties, especially for repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: First, while the Bill rightly strengthens the enforcement tools and registration requirements, I suggest that we consider a more graduated and targeted approach to penalties, especially for repeat offenders who knowingly disregard safety rules.

sections.label: Battery charging safety guidelines
sections.summary: Fires arise from uncertified batteries, unsafe modifications and overnight charging, so national charging-safety guidelines covering chargers, durations, zones and corridor charging are encouraged.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Many arise from uncertified batteries, unsafe modifications or prolonged overnight charging at unsuitable locations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: I encourage the introduction of national charging-safety guidelines, covering approved chargers, safe charging durations, designated charging zones and clear prohibitions against corridor charging.

sections.label: Traffic accidents and sentencing review
sections.summary: Singapore recorded 7,049 injury traffic accidents and over 100 fatalities in 2024, prompting an urge for a sentencing framework review for death by dangerous or drink-driving.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: In 2024, Singapore recorded 7,049 traffic accidents involving injuries, with more than 100 fatalities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: We have also seen cases where fatal outcomes arising from negligence or excessive speed resulted in sentences that, while legally consistent, have left the public uneasy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: I, therefore, urge the Ministry to consider a comprehensive review of sentencing frameworks, particularly for causing death by dangerous or drink-driving.

sections.label: New offence for unsafe devices
sections.summary: Part 6 of the Bill introduces a new offence of keeping an unsafe AMD by amending the Small Motorised Vehicle (Safety) Act 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On the new offence of possession of unsafe devices, Part 6 of the Bill will introduce a new offence of keeping an unsafe AMD by amending the Small Motorised Vehicle (Safety) Act 2020.

sections.label: AMD fires disproportionately fatal
sections.summary: On 12 January, responding to an Adjournment Motion by Andre Low, MHA confirmed AMD fires have been disproportionately fatal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On 12 January, in response to an Adjournment Motion filed by Workers' Party's Non-Constituency Member of Parliament Andre Low, MHA confirmed that AMD fires have been disproportionately fatal.

sections.label: Contractors to process traffic notices
sections.summary: Per MHA's 12 January media release, civilian contractors will process traffic notices for camera-detected violations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the MHA's media release of 12 January, civilian contractors will be tasked to process traffic notices for camera-detected violations.

sections.label: Who decides outsourcing appeals
sections.summary: The passage asks who will decide appeal cases when the provisions on outsourcing are activated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: When the provisions on outsourcing are activated, who will decide on appeal cases?

sections.label: Parliamentary Questions on device safety
sections.summary: The speaker asked seven questions on AMD safety, six on electrical battery safety and three on fire safety, filing 16 questions across MOT, MHA and MTI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Since debates commenced in this House in September, I have asked seven Parliamentary Questions on AMD safety, six Parliamentary Questions on electrical battery safety and three Parliamentary Questions on fire safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I filed a total of 16 questions across MOT, MHA and MTI, because one fire is a fire too many, especially in what is supposed to be a safe abode.

sections.label: Disabled People's Association certification recommendations
sections.summary: The Disabled People's Association recommended the Ministry ease medical certification and registration for genuine users through subsidies, assessor documentation instead of diagnosis, and broad assessment of medical need.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Disabled People's Association has recommended that the Ministry optimise inclusivity and ease the process for obtaining medical certification and registration for genuine users, such as by: (a) ensuring that grants or subsidies be established to cover any potential costs of certification and registration; (b) clarifying that the relevant "certification" needed does not require a formal medical diagnosis, but simply documentation from an assessor noting the need for the use of a PMA; and (c) ensuring that "medical need" to ride a PMA is assessed on a broad and inclusive basis.

sections.label: PMA speed limit lowered
sections.summary: A key development in this Bill is lowering the speed limit for PMAs from 10 kilometres per hour to six kilometres per hour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: A key development in this Bill lowering of the speed limit from 10 kilometres per hour to six kilometres per hour for PMAs.

sections.label: AMD fire risk and LTA regulations
sections.summary: MHA data shows AMDs caused over 25% of residential fire fatalities while under 5% of fires, mostly from illegally modified or uncertified devices, prompting LTA regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The disproportionate fire risk and danger of AMDs is widely recognised, with data shared by MHA revealing that while such devices accounted for less than 5% of residential fires in the past five years, they caused more than 25% of fatalities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I note that the bulk of these fires occurred from devices that were illegally modified, or those that were not tested and certified.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: To this end, LTA has implemented a series of regulations, such as the UL2272 standard and periodic inspections every two years for PMDs and the EN15194 standard for PABs.

sections.label: Support for Bill and implementation date
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill and looks forward to its implementation on 1 June 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding these clarifications, I support this Bill and look forward to the implementation on 1 June 2026.

sections.label: Bill strengthens PMA operating safety
sections.summary: The Bill reduces the PMA speed limit to six kilometres per hour by January 2029, extends size restrictions, requires registration and introduces a Certificate of Medical Need.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: That memory is still fresh in my mind and I do not want that to occur anymore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I note that this Bill seeks to strengthen the operating safety of PMAs by reducing the limit from 10 kilometres per hour to six kilometres per hour by January 2029, extending size restrictions, requiring registration and introducing a Certificate of Medical Need for the use of PMDs on public paths.

sections.label: Medical Need assessments and speeding violations
sections.summary: Speaker seeks clarification on whether Certificate of Medical Need assessments can be done at polyclinics, and notes 2024 speeding violations hit a 10-year high.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In particular, Sir, I seek clarification on whether assessments for the Certificate of Medical Need can be conducted at polyclinics so as to help manage costs and ensure accessibility.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In 2024, speeding violations reached a 10-year high, with the number of cases doubling compared to the previous year.

sections.label: Penalties for illegal vehicle modifications
sections.summary: Speaker welcomes stronger penalties for illegal vehicle modifications including speed limiter tampering, and urges companies to comply with speed limit rules by 1 July 2027.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I also welcome the strengthening of penalties for illegal vehicle modifications, including the tampering with speed limiters which undermine the intent of safety regulations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I urge companies to comply fully with the speed limit rules, including early installation ahead of the 1 July 2027 deadline.

sections.label: NTUC engagement on delivery worker regulations
sections.summary: NTUC and workers' associations met delivery workers to hear concerns about income, compliance costs and work routines, feeding into discussions with platform operators and agencies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: As a labour movement, NTUC takes seriously the impact of implementing these regulations on our workers' daily lives.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Through continuous engagement on the ground, NTUC and workers' associations, such as the National Delivery Champions Association (NDCA), have met delivery workers at their workplaces, where they rest, where they work, listening directly to concerns and worries they have about income, compliance costs and changes to their work routines.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Their feedback will form the basis for ongoing discussions with platform operators and relevant agencies, so that safety can be enhanced without sacrificing livelihoods.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Fair safety is safety that takes into account the reality of workers' lives.

sections.label: Certificate of Medical Need assessor unspecified
sections.summary: The Bill requires a Certificate of Medical Need but does not specify which doctor should assess it.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Bill requires a Certificate of Medical Need, but it does not specify which doctor should assess.

sections.label: Guidelines refinement after professional consultation
sections.summary: The guidelines are sound but need refinement, having been developed after consulting 11 professional bodies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, the guidelines are sound, but refinement will be needed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These were developed after consulting 11 professional bodies.

sections.label: Trusted reference and good faith assessors
sections.summary: The reference matured over years into a trusted one, and the FAQ clarifies assessors acting in good faith will not be second guessed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It matured over years, it is now a trusted reference.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I note that the "Frequently Asked Questions" (FAQ) clarifies that assessors acting in good faith will not be second guessed.

sections.label: Mobility vehicle registration with LTA
sections.summary: Devices had no equivalent gate when sold commercially, and mobility vehicles will now need registration with LTA.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When devices became available commercially, there was no equivalent gate.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am glad to note that mobility vehicles will now need to be registered with LTA.

sections.label: Measures for genuine mobility needs
sections.summary: Medical certification, lower speed limits and device registration aim to let those with genuine needs move safely and with dignity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The measures proposed – requiring medical certification, reducing speed limits and establishing device registration – serve to ensure that those with genuine needs can move safely and with dignity.

sections.label: Higher penalties for illegal vehicle alteration
sections.summary: Penalties for illegal alteration rise to $10,000 for individuals and $40,000 for corporates, with 72% of AMD-related fires involving non-compliant devices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The substantially increased penalties for illegal alteration of motorised vehicles, up to $10,000 for individuals and $40,000 for corporates, send a clearer signal on the non-negotiable ability of safety.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Seventy-two percent of AMD-related fires in the last three years were related to non-compliant devices, and I am glad that we are removing those safety hazards from our homes.

sections.label: Unpaid vehicle payments block renewals
sections.summary: Owners who do not pay what they owe cannot renew road tax or sell their vehicle until payments are settled.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: If vehicle owners do not pay what they owe, they would not be able to renew their road tax or sell their vehicle until the payments are settled.

sections.label: Graciousness and noise on public transport
sections.summary: Commuters can be mindful that personal music, loud phone conversations and unnecessary noise intrude on shared space.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Commuters can be mindful that personal music, loud phone conversations and unnecessary noise in public are intrusions on the shared space.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This is graciousness in its most equal form, the recognition that the time another person spent on public transport is as valuable as your own and that you have an obligation to protect their experience of that journey, that our homes and communities are places of rest and should be safe from noise and disruption.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: May we move forward with the understanding that a gracious transport system is one that accommodates all of our citizens, young and old, disabled and able-bodied, with equal care for their safety and dignity.

sections.label: Amendments to mobility vehicle definitions
sections.summary: Clauses 2(g), 2(h) and 16 amend the mobility scooter definition, add a mobility vehicles definition, and create an exception to the medical certificate offence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Clause 2(g) of the amendment Bill introduces certain amendments to the definition of a "mobility scooter", which emphasises that the mobility scooter should only have a "single seat behind the footboard".

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: However, clause 2(h) of the amendment Bill introduces a new definition of "mobility vehicles" to include "any other motor vehicle designed to carry an individual who is unable to walk or has difficulty in walking and prescribed for the purpose of this definition".

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In addition, clause 16 of the Amendment Bill introduces a new section 23I, which, in subsection (2), creates an exception to the offence of driving or riding a mobility vehicle without a certificate of medical need in circumstances prescribed in regulations.

sections.label: PMA speed limit reduction
sections.summary: The reduction of the PMA speed limit from 10 kilometres per hour to six kilometres per hour is sensible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The reduction of the PMA speed limit from 10 kilometres per hours to six kilometres per hour is sensible.

sections.label: AMD-related fires in HDB estates
sections.summary: MHA shared that 77, or 72%, of AMD-related fires in HDB estates in the past three years involved non-compliant or modified PMDs and PABs, meaning 28% involved compliant devices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: MHA shared recently that in the past three years, 77, or 72%, of the AMD-related fires in HDB estates involved PMDs and PABs which were either non-UL2272 compliant or non-EN15194 compliant; or had been modified, rendering them non-compliant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This means that a significant 28% or more than one in four AMD-related fires involved compliant devices.

sections.label: Reducing fire threat from devices
sections.summary: The speaker asks how the Government can reduce the threat given more than one in four fires are caused by compliant devices, and encourages a feasibility study on parking and charging in MSCPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: How can the Government reduce the threat to safety and property, given that more than one in four fires are caused by these compliant devices?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I encourage the agencies to conduct a feasibility study and share the study with public on allowing these devices to be parked at HDB Multi-storey Car Park (MSCP) as an option and to build fire-resistant charging infrastructure in MSCPs for users to charge their PMDs and PMA batteries.

sections.label: Speeding and EnterpriseSG support
sections.summary: Speeding remains a leading cause of fatal crashes, and the speaker commends EnterpriseSG for covering 50% of eligible costs for SMEs through the Productivity Solutions Grant.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Speeding remains one of the leading causes of fatal crashes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I commend EnterpriseSG for stepping in with support, covering 50% of eligible costs for small and medium enterprises through the Productivity Solutions Grant.

sections.label: Fires involving uncertified devices
sections.summary: Between 2022 and 2025, over 70% of such fires involved uncertified or illegally modified devices.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Between 2022 and 2025, over 70% of such fires involved uncertified or illegally modified devices.

sections.label: PMA speed and dimension limits
sections.summary: The reduction of PMA speed limits from 10 kilometres per hour to six is welcome, and dimension limits of 120 centimetres by 70 centimetres will prevent oversized devices from dominating shared paths.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The reduction of PMA speed limits from 10 kilometres per hour to six – the pace of brisk walking – is a welcome move.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Dimension limits of 120 centimetres by 70 centimetres, harmonised with public transport standards, will prevent oversized devices from dominating shared paths.

sections.label: E-scooter ban rider assistance
sections.summary: In 2019, when e-scooters were banned from footpaths, about 7,000 delivery riders were affected and the Government provided a $7 million transition assistance package.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In 2019, when e-scooters were banned from footpaths, approximately 7,000 delivery riders were affected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Recognising the impact on livelihoods, the Government provided a $7 million transition assistance package.

sections.label: Transition support for affected riders
sections.summary: The Minister of State is asked to clarify whether there will be transition support for affected riders and whether occupational factors can be considered.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Would the Minister of State clarify if there will be transition support for affected riders?

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Must it be a diagnosed medical condition, or can occupational factors be considered?

sections.label: Mobility vehicle definitions and registration
sections.summary: Clearer definitions of mobility vehicles, mandatory registration and a Certificate of Medical Need for certain devices strike a careful balance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The clearer definitions of mobility vehicles, together with mandatory registration and the requirement for a Certificate of Medical Need for certain devices, strike a careful balance.

sections.label: Upstream responsibility for unsafe devices
sections.summary: Compliance should come from understanding and support, and the Bill focuses on upstream responsibility with stronger controls on sale, advertisement and possession of unsafe devices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Compliance should come from understanding and support, not fear.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I also welcome the Bill's focus on upstream responsibility, particularly the stronger controls on the sale, advertisement and possession of unsafe or non-compliant devices.

sections.label: Offence for keeping unsafe devices
sections.summary: An offence for keeping unsafe devices reflects that risks arise before incidents, public education is essential, and mandatory disqualification periods are minimum periods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The introduction of an offence for keeping unsafe devices, even when they are not actively used, reflects an important reality that risks often arise long before an incident occurs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Clear public education will be essential so that people understand what is expected of them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I welcome the clarification that mandatory disqualification periods are minimum periods, restoring the original legislative intent following recent judicial interpretation.

sections.label: Land Transport Bill 2026 implementation
sections.summary: With careful implementation and continued engagement, the Land Transport and Related Matters Bill 2026 will strengthen the transport system and Singaporeans' confidence in it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With careful implementation and continued engagement, the Land Transport and Related Matters Bill 2026 will strengthen, not just our transport system, but also the confidence Singaporeans place in it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Preventing the misuse of PMAs by seemingly able-bodied individuals, tackling speeding and restricting the use of overly large devices, are good proposals by the AMAP and I am glad that the Government has adopted these recommendations.

sections.label: Fatal modified PMD lift fire
sections.summary: A man died in 2021 after his modified PMD burst into flames inside a lift.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Members may also remember the unfortunate 2021 incident, where a man died after his modified PMD burst into flames while he was inside a lift.

sections.label: Orchard Road lorry accident
sections.summary: A lorry accident on Orchard Road on 28 January 2026 sent 12 workers to hospital.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: More recently, an accident on 28 January 2026, that was just last week, involving a lorry along Orchard Road, resulted in 12 workers being sent to the hospital.

sections.label: Mandating seat belts
sections.summary: The speaker says seat belts should at least be mandated to protect passengers from being flung out in an accident.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In the meantime, we should, at the very least, mandate seat belts to protect passengers from being flung out of the vehicle in the event of an accident.

sections.label: PMA speed cap and shared paths
sections.summary: The Bill caps PMAs at six kilometres per hour on public paths, while bicycles, PMDs and PABs may still go 25 kilometres per hour.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: There are, however, a few points I would like to raise.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, the Bill will cap PMAs at six kilometres per hour on public paths.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: While we have restrained that one group of people with real medical needs to this relaxed pace, I must note that on our shared paths, bicycles, PMDs and PABs are still allowed to go 25 kilometres per hour, and I wonder why.

sections.label: Possession of non-UL2272 PMDs
sections.summary: Under this Bill, mere possession of non-UL2272 PMDs will also be an offence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: With this Bill, mere possession of non-UL2272 PMDs will also be an offence.

sections.label: Illegal modification and delivery earnings
sections.summary: A device illegally and unsafely modified to go faster translates into faster deliveries, shorter turnaround times, more completed orders and higher earnings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: A device illegally and unsafely modified to go faster translates directly into faster deliveries, shorter turnaround times and more completed orders and higher earnings.

sections.label: Errant AMDs and platform responsibility
sections.summary: Sections 23E and 23J of the Bill will hold platform companies responsible for workers using a mobility vehicle without a valid Certificate of Medical Need.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The problem of errant AMDs on our public spaces will remain intractable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I am particularly pleased to note that sections 23E and 23J of the Bill, which will hold platform companies responsible for their workers using a mobility vehicle without a valid Certificate of Medical Need.

sections.label: Matrix flagging unsafe behaviour
sections.summary: Simple matrix such as distance over time and turnaround time can flag excessive speed or unsafe behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Simple matrix, such as distance over time and turnaround time between delivery and pick-up, can easily flag excessive speed or unsafe behaviour.

sections.label: Platforms and unsafe riding rewards
sections.summary: Platforms should ensure their operational models do not systematically reward unsafe riding at the expense of public safety.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: While the Government can make and enforce rules, platforms should ensure that their operational models do not systematically reward unsafe riding at the expense of public safety.

sections.label: Riders pressured to take risks
sections.summary: A system pressurising riders to take risks to earn a decent income is neither fair nor acceptable, and NDCA is in discussion with delivery platforms for a fairer deal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: For their efforts, a system that pressurises riders to take risks just to earn a decent income is neither fair nor acceptable and I am glad to hear from the hon Member Ms Yeo Wan Ling that the NDCA is in discussion with such delivery platforms for a fairer deal.

sections.label: Subsidies and standardised clinical assessment
sections.summary: The Government is asked to consider subsidies for those in need to cover clinical assessment costs and how MOH will ensure standardised clinical practice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Will the Government consider providing subsidies for those in need to cover the cost of the clinical assessment?

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In addition, there were concerns that different medical practitioners may have differing practices in ascertaining the need, so how will MOH ensure standardised clinical practice?

sections.label: Streamlining process and financial subsidies
sections.summary: The Government is asked to streamline the process and consider subsidies or grants to cover registration and associated fees for those facing financial challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Will the Government be able to streamline the process to minimise the hassle for these persons and will the Government also consider the provision of subsidies or grants to cover the registration and associated fees for those among them that face financial challenges?

sections.label: Digital link for verification
sections.summary: The Government is asked to consider a seamless digital link between LTA's register and platform operator systems for automatic verification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In addition, though, will the Government consider a seamless digital link between LTA's register and the platform operator systems to facilitate automatic verification so that there is less doubt in between the processes?

sections.label: Mobility vehicle supply and speed
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked whether it considered centralising supply through healthcare institutions, and the six-kilometre-per-hour speed reduction is supported.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: And finally, given that the intent is for mobility vehicles to only be used by those with mobility challenges, did the Ministry consider centralising the supply through healthcare institutions only, for example?

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I support the reduction to six kilometres per hour, similar to Members like Mr Ng Shi Xuan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: A quick check online will show that while there is not a single global standard on what the speed should be, many jurisdictions, including the United Kingdom, including France, certain jurisdictions in Australia, in fact, Slovenia as well, recently ruled a new six-kilometre-per-hour for the use of mobility aids on pathways.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: So, that is, I believe a scientific consideration in the ascertainment of what the speed is.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: But the positive effect of all the changes we have in this Bill will only be felt by our residents on the ground if there is effective enforcement.

sections.label: Support for the Bill
sections.summary: The Member states that, despite the points raised, the Bill is supported.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the points I have raised, I support the Bill.

sections.label: Penalties for unauthorised modifications
sections.summary: Clause 52 strengthens penalties for unauthorised modifications, which the Member says is necessary.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Clause 52 strengthens penalties for unauthorised modifications and this is necessary.

sections.label: Fines and imprisonment message
sections.summary: The Bill raises penalties to fines of up to $20,000 and/or imprisonment, sending a message that personal preference cannot come at the expense of public safety.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: By raising penalties to fines of up to $20,000 and/or imprisonment, the Bill sends a clear message – personal preference cannot come at the expense of public safety and community well-being.

sections.label: Resident hit by PAB
sections.summary: Last December, a 71-year-old resident, Mrs Malar Singam, was knocked down by a power-assisted bicycle near Pasir Ris Mall.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Last December, a 71-year-old resident, Mrs Malar Singam, was knocked down by a power-assisted bicycle (PAB) near Pasir Ris Mall.

sections.label: Certificate of Medical Need safeguard
sections.summary: Clause 16 introduces a Certificate of Medical Need for PMA users, described as an important safeguard.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Clause 16 introduces a Certificate of Medical Need for PMA users, which is an important safeguard.

sections.label: Transitional measures for non-compliant devices
sections.summary: The Bill makes keeping non-compliant devices an offence, and the speaker hopes for transitional measures like buy-back or trade-in schemes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: As enforcement tightens, we should also support compliance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: This Bill makes it an offence to keep non-compliant devices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: I hope we can consider transitional measures such as buy-back or trade-in schemes that could help users shift to compliant devices, particularly where earlier purchases were made in good faith.

sections.label: Speed limits and installation subsidies
sections.summary: A resident SME operator suggested differentiating speed limits by vehicle class, and the speaker said the Productivity Solutions Grant should not fund regulatory compliance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: I support the safety intent behind this requirement, but at the same time, I wish to share feedback from a resident of mine who is also a small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) operator.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: She highlighted that further differentiation of speed limits by vehicle class could allow some more operational flexibility, especially for lower-weight lorries, specifically for those between 3,500 and 5,000 kilogrammes maximum laden weight, whose drivers often face punishing work schedules or reactive work orders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: On subsidies for encouraging installations, I would also like to point out that the Productivity Solutions Grant should be meant for genuine productivity uplift and not regulatory compliance like this one.

sections.label: Seniors exempted from medical certification
sections.summary: Seniors aged 70 and above will be exempted from medical certification, but those not exempted need a valid Certificate of Medical Need for mobility scooters.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: On this note, I am glad that seniors aged 70 and above will be exempted from the medical certification requirement.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: However, for those that are not exempted, such as those who are slightly below 70, the first hurdle that they would have to clear is having a valid Certificate of Medical Need to use a mobility scooter on public paths.

sections.label: LTA financial incentives power
sections.summary: The Bill states that LTA has the power to provide financial incentives, support, grants, aid and assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Against this backdrop, I am also heartened to know that the Bill also states that LTA has the power to provide financial incentives, support, grants, aid and assistance.

sections.label: NEHR medical certification data sharing
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether LTA will work with MOH to generate mobility scooter medical certification from previous records under mandatory NEHR data sharing.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: As we move towards mandatory data sharing for National Electronic Health Record (NEHR) system, will LTA consider working with the Ministry of Health (MOH) on how medical certification for mobility scooter can be generated based on previous records so that it reduces the friction or the need to see a physical doctor?

sections.label: Ramp power and rollback fears
sections.summary: A calculation suggests 158 watts is needed for a 90-kilogramme system on a 4.8-degree ramp at six kilometres per hour, and LTA is asked to reassure users about rollback.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Our back-of-the-envelope calculation suggests that for a 90-kilogramme system on a typical 4.8-degree ramp, 158 watts is needed to maintain at six kilometres per hour.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For many users, this fear is real: will I roll backwards at a slower speed?

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It would be helpful if LTA could also provide reassurance in terms of public communication that devices designed for public paths will not roll backwards on typical gradients, even at lower speeds.

sections.label: Communication and public suspicion
sections.summary: The speaker hopes LTA's communications make clear the intent is to prevent unsafe misuse, not encourage public policing, with enforcement guided by training and protocols.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: If the new regime unintentionally results in more public suspicion or harassment of legitimate users, it will undermine social trust.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I therefore hope LTA’s communications will be clear that the intent is to prevent unsafe misuse, not to encourage policing by all of us and by the public, and that enforcement will be guided by training and clear protocols.

sections.label: Consistent enforcement of safety rules
sections.summary: Safety rules must be stated and enforced consistently with resources and technology, and applied fairly so vulnerable users are not priced out of mobility.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Our safety rules must not only be stated but enforced consistently, supported with the right resources and technology, applied with fairness so that vulnerable users are not priced out of mobility.

sections.label: Certificate of Medical Need requirement
sections.summary: From June this year, users must have a Certificate of Medical Need to own a PMA, obtained after completing the Assessment for Mobility Scooter.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: From June this year, users must have the Certificate of Medical Need to own a PMA, which can only be obtained after completing the Assessment for Mobility Scooter (AMS) from doctors or occupational therapists.

sections.label: Reported PMA accident figures
sections.summary: From 2023 to Q3 2025, MOT said around 710 reported accidents involving PMAs, PMDs or PABs caused injuries, about 590 on roads and 120 off-road.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: From 2023 to Q3 2025, MOT said there were around 710 reported accidents involving PMAs, PMDs or PABs that resulted in injuries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And approximately 590 were on the roads and 120 were off-road, inclusive of public paths.

sections.label: Demerit system for PMA users
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Ministry can consider a demerit system for PMA users to deter repeat offenders who fail to consider others' safety.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry consider establishing a demerit system for PMA users to deter repeat offenders who fail to consider the safety of others?

sections.label: Mobility scooter assessment access and fees
sections.summary: Asks if MOT will coordinate with MOH and MSF on affordable assessment access and set a fee cap.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will the MOT coordinate with MOH and the MSF to ensure that existing and new mobility scooter users can easily access assessment services provided by doctors and occupational therapists at affordable prices?

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will the authorities set a fee cap for this service to avoid opportunistic price hiking?

sections.label: Mobility scooter assessment safety and time limits
sections.summary: Asks if assessments will evaluate safe operation and have time limits given health changes and ageing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will the assessment for mobility scooters include evaluating whether patients can safely operate the assistive device?

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Considering changes in their health conditions and the effects of ageing, will assessments have time limits for safety purposes?

sections.label: Fast-track certification after surgery or injury
sections.summary: Asks if there will be a fast-track or temporary certification process for residents needing a PMA after surgery or injury.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, will there be a fast-track or temporary certification process for residents who need a PMA after surgery or injury, ensuring rehabilitation does not become a compliance case?

sections.label: Polyclinic bottlenecks from mid-2026 rollout
sections.summary: Raises worry about bottlenecks at polyclinics with the rollout starting in mid-2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Second, with the rollout starting in mid-2026, I worry about bottlenecks at polyclinics.

sections.label: Offence for unregistered vehicle use
sections.summary: States section 28I creates an offence for using an unregistered vehicle and section 28M makes the register prima facie evidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Section 28I creates an offence for using an unregistered vehicle and section 28M makes the register prima facie evidence.

sections.label: Training and delivery-time management requirements
sections.summary: Asks why the Bill does not explicitly require training or delivery-time management, including algorithmic changes not rewarding speed over safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Second, why does the Bill not explicitly require training or delivery-time management, including algorithmic changes that do not reward speed at the expense of safety?

sections.label: Ang Mo Kio PMD fire
sections.summary: A PMD fire in a Block 641 Ang Mo Kio Avenue 4 lift lobby disrupted electrical supply and damaged lifts, which the passage says was avoidable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: On 4 November 2025, close to midnight, a fire broke out in the lift lobby of Block 641 Ang Mo Kio Avenue 4, involving a PMD.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Electrical supply was disrupted and lifts were damaged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: These disruptions were avoidable and they underline why prevention and enforcement matter.

sections.label: Certificate of Medical Need dignity
sections.summary: The passage states that on the Certificate of Medical Need, safety must never come at the cost of dignity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: On the Certificate of Medical Need, safety must never come at the cost of dignity.

sections.label: ERP 2.0 data platform
sections.summary: ERP 2.0 is a data and sensing platform whose new OBUs generate richer, more granular, real-time data for motorists and LTA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: At its core, ERP 2.0 is also a data and sensing platform.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The new OBUs generate richer, more granular and real-time data – both for motorists and the LTA.

sections.label: ERP 2.0 pricing limits
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister whether there will be clear limits, transparent criteria and regular public updates for adjusting ERP 2.0 pricing zones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It is, therefore, important to consider the overall impact of more granular road pricing and to ensure that flexibility does not create uncertainty for motorists or lead to higher costs without real congestion benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: So, may I ask the Minister whether there will be clear limits and transparent criteria for adjusting ERP 2.0 pricing zones, and regular public updates on congestion and travel times to ensure that flexibility delivers real improvements on the ground?

sections.label: Bill enforcement manpower costs
sections.summary: The passage asks about projected manpower requirements and costs from the Bill's expanded rules and enforcement, and plans to scale up automated enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Further, with the expansion of rules and enforcements introduced by this Bill, what are the projected manpower requirements and costs going forward and what immediate plans are in place to scale up automated enforcement to manage these constraints?

sections.label: Publishing clinics and fees
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry can regularly publish a list of clinics offering certification and update indicative fees to keep the process affordable and fair.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To ensure this does not unintentionally exclude those who need mobility support the most, can the Ministry regularly publish a clear list of clinics offering certification and update together with indicative fees, to enhance transparency and keep the process affordable and fair?

sections.label: Certificate of Medical Need concerns
sections.summary: Members support a Certificate of Medical Need to curb abuse, but caution about who may be left behind.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Second, while Members support the introduction of a Certificate of Medical Need to curb abuse, we must be clear-eyed about who we may have left behind.

sections.label: Flexible device implementation urged
sections.summary: The GPC urges flexible, affordable, clearly communicated implementation so complexities, cost or narrow definitions do not exclude or penalise dependent users.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
